toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.methodChoice: EDF v0.3 applied internally. Collected only X9 (rebuffering by app, version and ISP) and X10 (smart-TV 5.2 release and rollout record).
output.brief:
Kestria's buffering is almost certainly caused by our own smart-TV app 5.2, not Tessaline. Since 9 October, 5.2 has used a much smaller startup buffer (10 seconds down to 4) and switches quality sooner; Kestria was the only market given it. On Tessaline, 5.2 TV viewers stall about 5.9% of the time on all three ISPs, while web, phone and not-yet-updated TV viewers stay at 0.6–0.7%. Employee TVs on the old Corvane network showed the same fault before launch, and a QA ticket was deferred until after launch. Handball demand and ISP congestion don't fit the timing or the data. I'm about 95% sure.

Not established: whether buffering drove October's cancellations; the 1 October price rise is a rival explanation.

What to do: don't send the breach notice, withhold fees, switch back, or mute the alert. Revert the 5.2 streaming settings for Kestria (a per-market setting, about an hour) and hold the all-markets rollout planned for 20 November, which would otherwise spread this everywhere. Confirm stalls drop back to normal. Pause the win-back offer until we know why people left. Add app-version breakdowns to monitoring (about six weeks).
